subject: Final surge validation & sanity playbook for private VPC deployment
content:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: surge sanity playbook & network validation for NorthStar private VPC

Team — attaching the first cut of the ‘surge sanity’ playbook we want to run during the private VPC cutover with NorthStar. This is a focused checklist (canary + surge window validation) intended for the 2-hour maintenance window they approved.

High level:
- Canary (10m): 2 test app instances behind LB, ensure KV cache warm, run 500 concurrent inference calls with 2s p95 target.
- Surge (30m): scale to expected burst (x3 baseline), validate autoscaler behavior and GPU allocation.
- Network validation: verify NAT paths, intra-VPC egress to S3 endpoints, and VPC peer routes for telemetry.

Please review the playbook and the quick network diagnostics I attached (netdiag-20260812.txt). Key open questions:
1) Firewall rules: do we need to pre-provision the ephemeral ports used by the runtime control plane?
2) Fallback policy: confirm that the canary will automatically failover to hosted model if GPU pool returns 502/timeout.

Attachments: surge_sanity_playbook_v1.pdf (PDF, draft), netdiag-20260812.txt (txt)

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

---
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: surge sanity playbook & network validation for NorthStar private VPC

Karthik — quick notes inline (summary):
- Firewall/ports: yes, need 32768-61000/NAT ephemeral range opened for the runtime control-plane heartbeats (we ran into this on a customer POC). I pulled a snapshot of the current ACLs: netrules-snapshot.txt attached.
- S3 access: recommend pre-creating VPC endpoint and confirm IAM role ARN used by the deployment agent—otherwise first bootstrap will time out.
- Canary failover: the runtime will mark the model instance unhealthy after 3 consecutive 504s and will route to the hosted fallback. We should document the exact chase sequence (annotated in the playbook).

Small ask: can we add an explicit step to capture KV-cache warm metrics (time to warm and hit rate) as part of the canary? That metric will materially affect cold-starts during surge.

Attaching: netrules-snapshot.txt (ACL diff)

- Dev
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Proposed window: 15 Aug 2026, 02:00 - 04:00 UTC
Redwood attendees: Karthik, Dev, Rohan, Stephanie

- If canary passes, proceed to 30m surge and scale validation.
- If either step fails, Redwood will trigger the pre-agreed rollback to the staged hosted variant and restore traffic.

Deliverables after window: canary-results-20260815.csv, postdeploy-log-excerpts.txt, and a short TL;DR indicating acceptance or rollback.

Please reply with a one-line confirmation of the window and the app oncall contact.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sean O'Connor <sean.oconnor@northstarhealth.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@sysintegrators.io>, InfraOps <infra@northstarhealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 02:05:00 -0700
Subject: Canary kickoff & initial observations (NorthStar private VPC)

Team — short update from the canary run (attached raw outputs). This is chronological:
- 02:00 UTC: Canary started (2 app instances behind LB). We issued 500 concurrent inference calls over 10 minutes.
- 02:04 UTC: Observed transient NAT gateway re-association on one of the subnets (AWS reported brief ENI failover). ~1.2% of calls returned 503 during a 30s window. Failover path engaged successfully and no request-level timeouts exceeded our 5 minute abort.
- 02:15 UTC: KV-cache warm achieved at 92% hit-rate after 6s average warm-up. Dev’s metric capture looks good — attached canary-results-20260815.csv.
- 02:22 UTC: Surge initiated to x3 baseline. Autoscaler spiked GPU allocation as expected; one pod experienced an OOM on a non-production model loader — gracefully restarted; model inferences resumed under the fallback instance for ~40s.

Decision: Canary = PASS with minor infra notes (NAT re-association and loader OOM). We recommend proceeding to the full surge as planned but with two action items captured below.

Action items (short):
1) NorthStar: confirm that the ephemeral port range and NAT health checks are instrumented (we saw the ENI reassign; need post-mortem metric).
2) Redwood: add the model loader memory guard and bump the pod limit for non-prod loaders from 1.5Gi -> 2Gi (Dev has raised INFRA-9724).

Attachments: canary-results-20260815.csv, postdeploy-log-excerpts.txt

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Sean O'Connor <sean.oconnor@northstarhealth.com>, InfraOps <infra@northstarhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Post-deploy acceptance & next steps (NorthStar private VPC)

Thanks everyone — excellent run. Summary and acceptance:
- Canary PASS, Surge PASS (observed autoscaler behavior and acceptable p95 latency bump: baseline p95 140ms -> 210ms at peak).
- Known infra notes: NAT re-association (low impact), non-prod loader OOM (mitigated by restart and increased pod limit).

We consider this deployment validated for production traffic. Next steps:
1) Redwood to commit the model-loader pod limit change (INFRA-9724) — target deploy by 18 Aug 2026.
2) NorthStar to share post-window ENI/NAT health metrics for their audit (Sean).
3) Redwood will circulate the final playbook (surge_sanity_playbook_v1.pdf -> v2) with the appended run notes and a short TL;DR acceptance doc.

Closing note: please ack this message with either ACCEPT or ROLLBACK. If we see no rollback note by 23:59 UTC tonight, we will mark the cutover as accepted and proceed with routing the traffic per the agreed rollout policy.

- Rohan Mehta
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
